result.rule: Use end events for terminal outcomes. An end event has no outgoing sequence flow and is not the target of a message flow.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Use a terminate end only when all remaining activity in the current scope must end immediately.

Respect event positions: a none intermediate event is catch-only in normal flow and never on a boundary; link events are intermediate-only, thrown and caught in pairs at the same process level, and a catching link has no incoming sequence flow; terminate is an end event only.

Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.

args.text: When a process description narrates consecutive activities and ends with a final activity or outcome, connect the activities in the described order with sequence flows and connect the terminal activity to an end event.

result.rule: When the description presents activities in an order, states a decision outcome that leads to an activity, or identifies an event that determines what happens next.: Connect each stated transition with a sequence flow, including from the start event to the first activity, from each decision branch to its specified next step, and from an event-based gateway to its catching-event target.

When the description states a process start and an ordered sequence of activities or transitions between phases: Model the stated start, include each distinct activity, and connect the flow nodes with sequence flows in the described order, including transitions between phases.
When the description says that one activity uses or examines something produced by another activity: Connect the corresponding BPMN flow nodes with a sequence flow in the stated order.

When the description states distinct participant actions and their order, or describes outcomes that determine subsequent paths: Model each stated action as a corresponding BPMN activity, connect activities in the stated order, and represent outcome-dependent paths with appropriate gateways and flows.

result.rule: Create bpmn:collaboration when distinct participants interact and represent every participant as a bpmn:participant pool.
Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
Model performer information only when responsibility is stated. Prefer lanes for ordinary organizational responsibility.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
